findings.claim: The rejection of the merger rival is argued only from this side of the closing seam and never weighs the cross-seam catchword the row itself discloses, which argues continuity across the very seam the rival attacks.
findings.grounds: The row's closing seam is 1:3|1:4. device_notes discloses a catchword straddling it: בָּנִים֙ (oshb:Isa.1.2, token 8 of 13) against בָּנִ֖ים (oshb:Isa.1.4, token 9 of 19); the two carry different cantillation, so byte tier fails and the pair collates at accent_stripped tier exactly as the row names it, and the count object is right - the bare plural noun stands at 8 verses book-wide token-exact on re-sweep (sweep: 8 verses, skeleton, token-exact), where the naive contiguous-substring object returns 14 verses. The rejection field answers the rival from the summons imperatives שִׁמְע֤וּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ וְהַאֲזִ֣ינִי אֶ֔רֶץ (oshb:Isa.1.2, tokens 1-4, byte tier, re-collated) plus an asserted distinctness of speech-move; the far side's own bytes - the verse-initial ה֣וֹי (oshb:Isa.1.4, token 1, byte tier), which boundary_rationale does name as the seam signal - are never cited in the rejection, and the disclosed catchword is never weighed against the merger. The seam is not thereby shown wrong: the hoy onset is a ruled tier-1 signal standing in 1:4's own bytes, the cross-seam disclosure obligation is met in device_notes, and no tier-4 signal appears anywhere in the row as driver or corroboration.
findings.proposed_change: In strongest_rejected_alternative, ground the discriminator in the far-side bytes (the verse-initial ה֣וֹי at oshb:Isa.1.4, token 1, byte tier) and state why the accent_stripped-tier plural-noun catchword is a hinge rather than continuity; span unchanged.

findings.claim: A curly-quoted WEB English run in boundary_rationale is attributed to the MT witness, and that mis-prefix carried it past the mandatory verbatim gate.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale carries the survivor gloss “a very small remnant” tagged (oshb:Isa.1.9); the run is WEB English (web:Isa.1.9), not MT bytes. Re-run of the staged verbatim gate over the eight rows as shipped counts 15 curly-quoted English runs checked out of 19 present; re-tagging exactly the four English runs that carry oshb: refs (at 1:9, 1:17, 1:20 and 1:31) to web: refs raises the gate to 19 checked, 0 flags. Each run is therefore verbatim WEB and the defect is confined to the witness prefix, which is what suppressed the check. The row's Hebrew and mark evidence at that verse re-verifies clean: הוֹתִ֥יר stands at token 4 and שָׂרִ֖יד at token 6 of oshb:Isa.1.9 (11 tokens), both byte tier, and both sit outside the four-way remnant family as the row states; the mark at Isa.1.9 is SAMEKH in the inventory under the claimed setumah type, single-witness and tier-3 as disclosed, and it is carried beside the tier-1 imperative onset at 1:10 rather than as the driver; and the place-name digits are exact - the Sodom skeleton at 4 verses and the Gomorrah skeleton at 3 verses book-wide (sweep: 4 verses / 3 verses, skeleton), with adjacent-verse co-occurrence at 1:9|1:10 only, the third shared site carrying both names inside one verse.
findings.proposed_change: Re-tag the English run as (web:Isa.1.9); no other field changes, span unchanged.

findings.claim: The closing imperative-catalogue gloss is a WEB English run attributed to the MT witness, bypassing the verbatim gate.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale sets the closing imperative-catalogue gloss - a WEB English run belonging to web:Isa.1.17 - under the tag (oshb:Isa.1.17). Re-run of the staged verbatim gate over the eight rows as shipped counts 15 curly-quoted English runs checked out of 19 present; re-tagging exactly the four English runs that carry oshb: refs (at 1:9, 1:17, 1:20 and 1:31) to web: refs raises the gate to 19 checked, 0 flags. Each run is therefore verbatim WEB and the defect is confined to the witness prefix, which is what suppressed the check. The setumah cited at that verse is right: the inventory records SAMEKH at Isa.1.17, single-witness, and the row discloses tier-3.
findings.proposed_change: Re-tag the English run as (web:Isa.1.17); span unchanged.

findings.claim: The opening warrant labels its splice a double imperative, but the quoted run carries only the first imperative and the WEB gloss beside it covers the whole verse.
findings.grounds: The splice שִׁמְע֥וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה קְצִינֵ֣י סְדֹ֑ם is tokens 1-5 of oshb:Isa.1.10 (10 tokens, byte tier re-collated); the second imperative הַאֲזִ֛ינוּ is token 6, outside the run, while the English gloss set beside it (web:Isa.1.10) renders all ten tokens. The verse's own bytes do carry the pair, so the double-imperative claim is not byte-false and the seam signal is genuinely tier-1 in the cited verse; the quoted extent under-covers the claim it is offered to ground, and the form-class contrast with 1:2 argued in device_notes (plural human addressee against the feminine-singular form) is byte-checkable and holds.
findings.proposed_change: Extend the splice through token 6 of oshb:Isa.1.10, הַאֲזִ֛ינוּ, so the run carries the pair it is cited for, or re-label the quoted run as the first member of the pair; span unchanged.

findings.claim: strongest_rejected_alternative carries a positional row reference where campaign register requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored.
findings.grounds: The field opens 'Reading verses 10-17 as a continuation of the row-3 indictment rather than a new unit was rejected'; 'the row-3 indictment' is a positional row reference whose referent is the 1:4-1:9 unit. Register purge bars positional row references in row prose in every field and requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored. No staged gate covers this arm - the citation, mark, quote, refs-mirror, tiling and cross-row n-gram checks all return GREEN over the eight rows as shipped - so the escape is silent.
findings.proposed_change: Replace 'the row-3 indictment' with the verse-anchored form (for example 'the 1:4-1:9 indictment'); span unchanged.

findings.claim: The closing-formula gloss is a WEB English run attributed to the MT witness, bypassing the verbatim gate.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale carries “for Yahweh’s mouth has spoken it.” tagged (oshb:Isa.1.20); the run is WEB English (web:Isa.1.20), and the Hebrew of the same formula is separately and correctly spliced beside it. Re-run of the staged verbatim gate over the eight rows as shipped counts 15 curly-quoted English runs checked out of 19 present; re-tagging exactly the four English runs that carry oshb: refs (at 1:9, 1:17, 1:20 and 1:31) to web: refs raises the gate to 19 checked, 0 flags. Each run is therefore verbatim WEB and the defect is confined to the witness prefix, which is what suppressed the check. Everything else in the row re-verifies exact: תְּאֻכְּל֔וּ כִּ֛י פִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה stands at tokens 5-8 of oshb:Isa.1.20 and recurs byte-identically at oshb:Isa.40.5 and oshb:Isa.58.14 (sweep: 3 verses, byte), all three in the ki-form; the quotative object splits exactly as claimed - the bare form at 5 verses (oshb:Isa.1.11, oshb:Isa.1.18, oshb:Isa.33.10, oshb:Isa.41.21, oshb:Isa.66.9) against 5 vav-prefixed narrative-onset sites - and the 1:18 and 1:11 forms collate at accent_stripped tier as named, with the 1:18 occurrence at tokens 4-5 as stated; the marks at Isa.1.17 and Isa.1.20 are SAMEKH in the inventory, single-witness, tier-3 disclosed, and stand as corroboration beside a tier-1 byte signal, never as the driver.
findings.proposed_change: Re-tag the English run as (web:Isa.1.20); span unchanged.

findings.claim: The stated rejection of the 1:23|1:24 rival weighs the inclusio only against the tier-3 parashah witness and never against the tier-1 divine-speech frame the row itself names as the rival's other ground.
findings.grounds: strongest_rejected_alternative builds the rival on two grounds - the petuchah at the close of verse 23 and the neum turn at verse 24 - then rejects it because the bracket is 'a stronger, byte-grounded cohesion signal than a single tier-3 parashah witness', and device_notes adds that the rejection 'rests on the skeleton-tier inclusio bracket alone, not on the signature's position'. The neum stack is a ruled tier-1 divine-speech frame, not a tier-3 mark: נְאֻ֤ם הָֽאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת stands at tokens 2-5 of oshb:Isa.1.24 (12 tokens, byte tier re-collated, after the connective לָכֵ֗ן and ahead of אֲבִ֖יר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל at tokens 6-7), and it is left unweighed in the comparison actually stated. The row's own digits are exact on re-sweep and do support its handling: the signature stands at 23 verses book-wide (sweep: 23 verses, skeleton) and is verse-initial at exactly one site, oshb:Isa.56.8, so the 1:24 occurrence is postpositive rather than an onset; and the inclusio קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָ֑ה (oshb:Isa.1.21, tokens 4-5) against קִרְיָ֖ה נֶאֱמָנָֽה (oshb:Isa.1.26, tokens 12-13) collates at skeleton tier only - the meteg retained at 1:26 blocks accent_stripped - standing at 2 verses book-wide, exactly as the row names it. The mark types are right too: PE at Isa.1.23 cited as petuchah, never conflated with the SAMEKH sites at 1:20 and 1:17. The span is not shown wrong; the rejection comparison is incomplete.
findings.proposed_change: In strongest_rejected_alternative, weigh the rival's tier-1 component explicitly - the postpositive, non-verse-initial position of the neum signature at oshb:Isa.1.24 (token 2 of 12) against its single verse-initial site book-wide - alongside the tier-3 witness; span unchanged.

findings.claim: The WEB gloss set beside the neum splice renders two tokens the splice does not cover.
findings.grounds: The splice נְאֻ֤ם הָֽאָדוֹן֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת is tokens 2-5 of oshb:Isa.1.24; the WEB gloss beside it (web:Isa.1.24) renders tokens 1-7, adding לָכֵ֗ן at token 1 and אֲבִ֖יר יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל at tokens 6-7. Both the splice and the gloss are separately correct at their own witnesses and the gloss is verbatim WEB under the staged gate; only the extents differ.
findings.proposed_change: Extend the splice to tokens 1-7 of oshb:Isa.1.24, or trim the gloss to the stacked title-and-signature it is cited for; span unchanged.

findings.claim: The cross-seam disclosure carried in device_notes names a seam this row does not own, while the device it describes straddles this row's own opening seam.
findings.grounds: The orphan/widow bracket links oshb:Isa.1.17 (יָת֔וֹם token 8, אַלְמָנָֽה token 10) to oshb:Isa.1.23 (יָתוֹם֙ token 10, אַלְמָנָ֖ה token 14); on re-verification the orphan noun matches at accent_stripped tier and the widow noun at skeleton tier only - the meteg retained at 1:17 blocks accent_stripped - standing at 2 and 3 verses book-wide token-exact, all four values exactly as the row states. 1:23 lies inside this row's span 1:21-1:26 and 1:17 lies upstream of it, so the device straddles this row's own opening seam at 1:20|1:21; the disclosure instead reads 'not cross-seam cohesion at 1:17|1:18', which is the neighbouring 1:10-1:17 row's seam, and the sentence is carried over from that row near-verbatim. Every site, tier and digit is present, so nothing is concealed; the seam addressed is not this row's.
findings.proposed_change: Re-frame the disclosure to this row's own front seam at 1:20|1:21, keeping the sites, tiers and digits as they stand; span unchanged.

findings.claim: The row's only opening-seam driver is a Hebrew form-class claim - a first-person to third-person discourse-mode shift - argued with no pointed splice of the verb forms it rests on.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale rests the 1:26|1:27 seam on the shift from the first-person divine speech of 1:24-26 to third-person declarative summary, and strongest_rejected_alternative concedes the seam 'is argued from this mode shift alone, with no explicit lexical frame marker'. The claim is byte-true - oshb:Isa.1.26 opens וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה (token 1 of 13) and the verb of oshb:Isa.1.27 is תִּפָּדֶ֑ה (token 3 of 5) - but neither form is spliced anywhere in the row: the seam's label is carried by an English rendering, while the only pointed evidence the row offers at this seam is the righteousness catchword, which it correctly reports as straddling the seam, that is, as material pulling the other way. Campaign law makes the pointed splice with its tier mandatory for a boundary-relevant original-language claim, and form-class labels carry the same discipline as digits. Confidence is held at medium_low with the frontier flag set, which is the calibrated handling for a mode-shift-only seam, so the seam is under-evidenced in the row rather than shown wrong, and no tier-4 signal is used as driver or corroboration anywhere in the row.
findings.proposed_change: Splice the two verb forms at byte tier into boundary_rationale - וְאָשִׁ֤יבָה (oshb:Isa.1.26, token 1) against תִּפָּדֶ֑ה (oshb:Isa.1.27, token 3) - as the pointed ground of the person shift; span unchanged.

findings.claim: The closing citation attributes a WEB English run to the MT witness and glosses one token more than its splice covers.
findings.grounds: The splice runs tokens 1-6 of oshb:Isa.1.31 (10 tokens), ending וּבָעֲר֧וּ; the English beside it, “They will both burn”, renders a plural-pair word that answers to שְׁנֵיהֶ֛ם at token 7, outside the splice. That same English run is tagged (oshb:Isa.1.31) although it is WEB text (web:Isa.1.31). Re-run of the staged verbatim gate over the eight rows as shipped counts 15 curly-quoted English runs checked out of 19 present; re-tagging exactly the four English runs that carry oshb: refs (at 1:9, 1:17, 1:20 and 1:31) to web: refs raises the gate to 19 checked, 0 flags. Each run is therefore verbatim WEB and the defect is confined to the witness prefix, which is what suppressed the check. The row's other evidence re-verifies exact: the mark at Isa.1.31 is SAMEKH in the inventory, single-witness, tier-3 as disclosed; the adjacent-verse righteousness catchword sits at oshb:Isa.1.26 token 11 and oshb:Isa.1.27 token 5 as stated, and is disclosed as straddling the row's own front seam; and the justice/righteousness co-occurrence object stands at 16 verses book-wide and at exactly 2 verses in this chapter, oshb:Isa.1.21 and oshb:Isa.1.27 (sweep: 16 verses / 2 verses, skeleton).
findings.proposed_change: Re-tag the English run as (web:Isa.1.31) and extend the splice through token 7 of oshb:Isa.1.31, שְׁנֵיהֶ֛ם, so gloss extent equals splice extent; span unchanged.

findings.claim: The row declares a parashah closure signal although no mark stands anywhere in its span; the mark it cites is at a verse outside the row.
findings.grounds: observed_substrate_signals carries parashah.samekh_boundary while the span is Isa.2.1-Isa.2.1. The mark inventory records no seg at Isa.2.1 - the chapter 1-2 marks are SAMEKH at 1:9, 1:17, 1:20 and 1:31, PE at 1:23, PE at 2:4, SAMEKH at 2:11 and PE at 2:22 - so the setumah the row cites stands at oshb:Isa.1.31, outside the span. The prose disclosure of that mark is itself correct (single-witness, tier-3, corroboration), so the defect is confined to the declared signal key, which asserts a substrate boundary signal the row's own verse does not carry; the neighbouring 1:10-1:17 row, whose closing verse does carry a SAMEKH, declares no parashah key at all, so the practice is not uniform across the slice. Recorded without adjudication: the audit brief bars parashah.* keys outright while the owner-ruled strategy's field contract lists parashah.* among the sanctioned dotted keys - under the brief's stricter reading the same finding would extend to the parashah keys in the 1:4-1:9, 1:18-1:20, 1:21-1:26 and 1:27-1:31 rows, whose devices do at least stand inside their own spans.
findings.proposed_change: Drop parashah.samekh_boundary from observed_substrate_signals, leaving the prose disclosure of the 1:31 mark as it stands; span unchanged.

findings.claim: The corroboration sentence attaches the 1:31 mark to the wrong seam.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale names the row's own seam as the one at 2:1|2:2 ('verse 2 opens a fresh eschatological formula ... which is the row's own seam'), then says 'Immediately upstream of that seam, 1:31 closes with a setumah break of its own'. oshb:Isa.1.31 is immediately upstream of the row's front seam at 1:31|2:1, not of the 2:1|2:2 seam the sentence attaches it to; the clause that follows ('corroborating the division from the chapter that precedes it') shows the front seam is what was meant. The mark fact itself is right - SAMEKH at Isa.1.31 in the inventory, single-witness, tier-3 disclosed, corroboration only - and the row's own seam signal at 2:2 is named with its ref rather than argued from any tier-4 fact.
findings.proposed_change: Attach the corroboration to the front seam explicitly (immediately upstream of this row's own front seam at 1:31|2:1); span unchanged.

findings.claim: device_notes rules out a copying variant, a transmission claim the staged single-witness evidence cannot support.
findings.grounds: The field asserts that the header-noun contrast with 1:1 is 'a genuine lexical distinction, not a copying variant'. The contrast itself is byte-true - חֲזוֹן֙ at token 1 of oshb:Isa.1.1 against הַדָּבָר֙ at token 1 of oshb:Isa.2.1 - but the staged substrate is a single MT witness and every other textual tradition is barred from evidentiary use, so no available evidence can exclude a variant; the negative claim is unsourceable rather than false. The three tier claims in the same field are exact on re-collation: אֲשֶׁ֣ר חָזָ֔ה collates at byte tier (oshb:Isa.1.1 tokens 5-6 against oshb:Isa.2.1 tokens 2-3, and 3 verses book-wide with oshb:Isa.13.1, sweep: 3 verses, byte); the seer's name collates at accent_stripped tier, the retained meteg leaving only the cantillation to differ; and the patronymic collates at skeleton tier only - בֶן at oshb:Isa.1.1 token 3 carries no dagesh against בֶּן at oshb:Isa.2.1 token 5, with the name's accent differing as stated.
findings.proposed_change: Delete 'not a copying variant', or re-cast it as a claim about the two headers' attested forms in the staged witness; span unchanged.
